note: 'Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them.' (Lev 9:22), and with Moses again at 9:23.

Set out in Leviticus 23 (23:34); kept on the return from exile: 'The whole assembly that had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated like this' (Neh 8:17).
Set out in Leviticus 23 (23:6); kept after the temple was rebuilt: 'For seven days they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy' (Ezra 6:22).

One of the feasts of the Lord set out in Leviticus 23, which gathers them into a single calendar: 'These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies' (23:2).; 'They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, in the wilderness of Sinai'; Kept the night the firstborn died, and instituted in the same chapter (Exod 12:28).
Set out in Leviticus 23 (23:3); first kept in the wilderness: 'So the people rested on the seventh day' (Exod 16:30).

'You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, or else you will die' (Lev 10:8-9). **One of the few times the Lord speaks to Aaron directly** rather than through Moses, and it comes immediately after his sons die.

'Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire in them and added incense, and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, contrary to His command. So fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them' (Lev 10:1-2). **Fire offered and fire returned**, in two verses, and the book does not say what made the fire strange.

'Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them. Fire came out from before the LORD, and devoured them' (Lev 10:1-2). **Fire offered and fire returned**, in two verses, and the book does not say what made the fire strange.

'He also poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him' (Lev 8:12), and again with blood from the altar at 8:30. **Moses consecrates the priesthood he does not hold**, which the book states without remarking on it.

'Approach the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering to make atonement for yourself and for the people' (Lev 9:7). **For yourself first**, and the order is the point.; 'Do not let your hair become disheveled and do not tear your garments, or else you will die' (Lev 10:6), said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar over the bodies of the other two. **They are forbidden to mourn**, and Aaron's answer to the whole thing at 10:3 is one clause: 'But Aaron remained silent.'

'Take the blasphemer outside the camp ... have the whole assembly stone him' (Lev 24:14), carried out at 24:23. **The verse before has him put in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them** (24:12), so the sentence is not Moses's own.
